findings.passage: “We have a responsibility to our citizens to ensure every vote cast is a legitimate, legal vote. If even one person votes illegally, it cancels out a legal voter’s choice to lead our communities, state and nation.”
findings.note: Press release on reintroducing his bill (House Bill 1061) to require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote; he links it to the federal SAVE Act and to automatic voter registration.

findings.passage: “I, too, want to see every single eligible Pennsylvanian registered to vote and casting ballots in every election,” Warner said. “But we must be thorough in protecting the rights of legal voters and the legitimacy of the ballots they cast.”
findings.note: Same release; says he wants all eligible people registered while protecting ballot legitimacy.

findings.passage: “Free and fair elections are the backbone of our republic, and it is paramount we do all we can to protect our elections and secure the integrity of our election administration,” Warner said. “This includes ensuring only qualified electors are registered to vote.”
findings.note: Release on introducing House Bill 2629 (proof of citizenship to register), as quoted in a caucus release in his name.

findings.passage: For example, House Bill 891 would give YOU the opportunity to decide whether the state should require voters to present identification each time they cast their ballots. Voter ID has broad, bipartisan support among the majority of Pennsylvanians.
findings.note: August 2024 newsletter; describes a bill to put a voter ID requirement to voters as a constitutional question and says voter ID is widely supported. Date is the newsletter's August 2024 edition (day unknown).

findings.passage: I am introducing legislation modeled after the SAVE Act, which would require people to provide proof of citizenship to register to vote.
findings.note: Same newsletter; announces proof-of-citizenship bill modeled on the federal SAVE Act.

findings.passage: “I am calling for a prompt investigation into this failure of the Department of State and will be working with other lawmakers to ensure accountability and that voters will not be disenfranchised again.”
findings.note: Statement after electronic pollbook problems in Fayette County turned voters away; about voter-roll data, not ID.

findings.passage: “We owe it to every single voter in Pennsylvania – regardless of their party affiliation – to conduct this audit to help ensure the integrity of this election and all future elections,” Warner said.
findings.note: Release praising House Resolution 1100 for an audit of the 2020 election; also cites concerns about mail-in ballots.
